name: Doji
formation: Open and close are (almost) the same, so the body is a thin line. The wicks can be long or short.
reading: Neither buyers nor sellers won the period: a sign of indecision. After a long, strong move, some traders read it as a warning that the move is losing energy.
confirmation: Most traders wait for the next candle: a strong move away from the doji in one direction tells more than the doji itself.
failure: Dojis are very common. In a quiet market or on short timeframes they often mean nothing at all.

name: Long-legged doji
formation: A doji with long wicks on both sides: price moved far up and far down but closed where it opened.
reading: Strong tug-of-war with no winner. Read as heightened indecision.
confirmation: A clear break above the high or below the low of the doji.
failure: Price often just keeps moving in the original direction once the indecision is resolved.

name: Dragonfly doji
formation: Open, close and high are at (almost) the same level at the top; there is a long lower wick and little or no upper wick.
reading: Sellers pushed price down, but buyers brought it all the way back by the close. After a decline it is traditionally read as a possible bullish reversal.
confirmation: A higher close on the next candle.
failure: If the next candle falls below the dragonfly's low, the rejection of lower prices has failed.

tested.theory: Bullish reversal during a decline, otherwise indecision

name: Gravestone doji
formation: Open, close and low are at (almost) the same level at the bottom; there is a long upper wick and little or no lower wick.
reading: Buyers pushed price up, but sellers brought it all the way back down. After a rise it is traditionally read as a possible bearish reversal.
confirmation: A lower close on the next candle.
failure: If the next candle closes above the gravestone's high, the rejection failed and the uptrend continues.

name: Spinning top
formation: A small body in the middle of the candle, with upper and lower wicks that are longer than the body.
reading: Both sides were active but neither took control: indecision, similar to a doji but with a slightly larger body.
confirmation: The direction of the next decisive candle.
failure: Spinning tops are among the most frequent candles; on their own they carry little information.

name: Marubozu
formation: A long body with no (or almost no) wicks: a bullish marubozu opens at the low and closes at the high; a bearish one opens at the high and closes at the low.
reading: One side was in control from the first trade to the last. Traditionally read as strong momentum in the direction of the body.
confirmation: Follow-through in the same direction on the next candle.
failure: A strong candle can mark the end of a move (a final burst of buying or selling), after which price reverses.

name: Hammer
formation: A small body at the top of the candle, a long lower wick (traditionally at least twice the body) and little or no upper wick, appearing after a decline.
reading: Sellers pushed price well down during the period, but buyers bought it back up to near the open. Traditionally read as a possible bullish reversal.
confirmation: A higher close on the next candle; some traders also want higher volume.
failure: If price falls below the hammer's low, the buyers' defence has failed.

name: Hanging man
formation: The same shape as a hammer (small body at the top, long lower wick) but appearing after a rise.
reading: Sellers managed to push price far down during the period: a sign that buying pressure may be weakening. Traditionally read as a possible bearish reversal.
confirmation: A lower close on the next candle.
failure: This pattern often fails: the uptrend frequently just continues.

name: Inverted hammer
formation: A small body at the bottom of the candle with a long upper wick and little or no lower wick, appearing after a decline.
reading: Buyers tried to push price up but could not hold the gains. After a decline, traditionally read as a first sign that buyers are testing higher prices.
confirmation: A higher close on the next candle is usually required before anyone reads anything into it.
failure: Without confirmation the decline often continues.

name: Shooting star
formation: A small body at the bottom of the candle with a long upper wick and little or no lower wick, appearing after a rise.
reading: Buyers pushed price higher, but sellers took over and drove it back near the open. Traditionally read as a possible bearish reversal.
confirmation: A lower close on the next candle.
failure: If price closes above the shooting star's high, the rejection has failed.

name: Bullish engulfing
formation: Two candles after a decline: a bearish candle followed by a bullish candle whose body completely covers (engulfs) the first body.
reading: Sellers were in control, then buyers took over decisively. Traditionally read as a possible bullish reversal.
confirmation: Further gains on the following candle(s).
failure: If price drops back below the low of the pattern, the reversal has failed.

name: Bearish engulfing
formation: Two candles after a rise: a bullish candle followed by a bearish candle whose body completely covers the first body.
reading: Buyers were in control, then sellers took over decisively. Traditionally read as a possible bearish reversal.
confirmation: Further losses on the following candle(s).
failure: If price climbs back above the high of the pattern, the reversal has failed.

name: Bullish harami
formation: Two candles after a decline: a long bearish candle followed by a small bullish candle whose body sits inside the first body. ('Harami' is Japanese for pregnant.)
reading: The strong selling has paused. Traditionally read as a possible bullish reversal, though weaker than an engulfing pattern.
confirmation: A close above the first candle's body.
failure: Often the pause is only a breather before the decline continues.

name: Bearish harami
formation: Two candles after a rise: a long bullish candle followed by a small bearish candle whose body sits inside the first body.
reading: The strong buying has paused. Traditionally read as a possible bearish reversal.
confirmation: A close below the first candle's body.
failure: Often the uptrend simply continues after the pause.

name: Harami cross
formation: A harami whose second candle is a doji, sitting inside the body of a long first candle. Shown here after a decline (bullish version); the bearish version appears after a rise.
reading: A long move is followed by complete indecision. Traditionally read as a stronger hint of a turn than a normal harami.
confirmation: A decisive move in the opposite direction of the first candle.
failure: The indecision is frequently resolved in the original direction.

name: Piercing line
formation: Two candles after a decline: a long bearish candle, then a bullish candle that opens below the first candle's low and closes above the middle of the first body.
reading: A weak open was met by strong buying that recovered more than half of the previous loss. Traditionally read as a possible bullish reversal.
confirmation: Further gains, ideally a close above the first candle's open.
failure: If the next candles fall back below the second candle's low, the pattern has failed.

name: Dark cloud cover
formation: Two candles after a rise: a long bullish candle, then a bearish candle that opens above the first candle's high and closes below the middle of the first body.
reading: A strong open was met by heavy selling that erased more than half of the previous gain. Traditionally read as a possible bearish reversal.
confirmation: Further losses, ideally a close below the first candle's open.
failure: If price recovers above the second candle's high, the pattern has failed.

name: Morning star
formation: Three candles after a decline: a long bearish candle, a small candle (the 'star') that trades lower, then a long bullish candle that closes well into the first candle's body.
reading: Selling, then hesitation, then strong buying. Traditionally read as a possible bullish reversal.
confirmation: The third candle itself is the confirmation; some traders also want higher volume on it.
failure: A fall below the star's low cancels the reading.

name: Evening star
formation: Three candles after a rise: a long bullish candle, a small candle (the 'star') that trades higher, then a long bearish candle that closes well into the first candle's body.
reading: Buying, then hesitation, then strong selling. Traditionally read as a possible bearish reversal.
confirmation: The third candle itself is the confirmation.
failure: A rise above the star's high cancels the reading.

name: Three white soldiers
formation: Three long bullish candles in a row, each opening within the previous body and closing near its high, after a decline or a quiet period.
reading: Steady, persistent buying over three periods. Traditionally read as a strong bullish signal.
confirmation: Continued strength; a close below the third candle's body weakens the signal.
failure: After three strong candles the market is often stretched and may pull back.

name: Three black crows
formation: Three long bearish candles in a row, each opening within the previous body and closing near its low, after a rise.
reading: Steady, persistent selling over three periods. Traditionally read as a strong bearish signal.
confirmation: Continued weakness; a close above the third candle's body weakens the signal.
failure: After three strong down candles the market may be oversold and bounce.

name: Tweezer bottom
formation: Two (or more) candles after a decline with (almost) the same low.
reading: Sellers failed twice at the same price: traders read it as a support level being defended.
confirmation: A higher close afterwards.
failure: A break below the shared low turns the 'support' into a failed level.

name: Tweezer top
formation: Two (or more) candles after a rise with (almost) the same high.
reading: Buyers failed twice at the same price: traders read it as a resistance level holding.
confirmation: A lower close afterwards.
failure: A break above the shared high means the resistance did not hold.

name: Inside bar
formation: A candle whose high and low are both inside the range of the previous candle.
reading: The market is pausing and the range is contracting. Traders watch which side of the larger candle's range breaks first.
confirmation: A close beyond the high or low of the first (larger) candle.
failure: Breakouts from tight ranges are often false: price breaks one side, then reverses.
